findings.title: website_name leaks hidden website info for anonymous TL0 users
findings.body: `website_name` was added to the serialized attributes but was not added to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111). `website_name` is derived from `website`, so even when the existing untrusted-attribute restriction suppresses the `website` key for anonymous visitors viewing a TL0 profile, the serializer still computes and emits `website_name`. This reveals the host and path of a website that is supposed to be hidden. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and make sure any manual `include_website_name?` does not override the generated restriction; the spec's untrusted attributes list should also be updated.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing `?` and has no effect
findings.body: ActiveModel Serializer conditional inclusion methods are named `include_<attribute>?` (see `include_email?` and `include_stats?` in this same file). The new method is `def include_website_name` without the trailing question mark, so it is never consulted during serialization. As a result, `website_name` is always included, producing `website_name: null` for users with no website or an unparsable website value instead of omitting the key. Rename it to `include_website_name?` or remove it in favor of the generated untrusted-attributes include method.
